A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SHeaP work and have readable text, equations, figures and tables. Each contains eight main-text pages followed by three reference pages. Neither supplied PDF contains appendices, although both mention supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results on NoW and Nersemble, emotion-prediction results on AffectNet, and component ablations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results and adds a graph-disabled ablation in Table 4, alongside revised qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The ViT, UV generator, graph network, densification/pruning, binding, shading and losses remain the same. Correcting the Gaussian parameter total from 13 to 14 leaves the listed component dimensions unchanged. The graph-disabled variant is an ablation, not a replacement of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on VFHQ and Nersemble and evaluate reconstruction on NoW/Nersemble and emotion prediction on AffectNet. The replacement portrait examples and added graph ablation do not establish a new task, domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 4 replaces Deep3DFaceRecon with AlbedoGAN while retaining DECA, EMOCA and SMIRK. AlbedoGAN already appeared in Table 1, but its participation in this qualitative comparison is new. The quantitative benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added NoW-validation control disables all graph edges, producing an MLP-style ResNet while retaining the other tabulated components. Existing dataset sampling, evaluation metrics, resolutions, learning rates and fixed-FOV setting remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 and Table 4 add an ablation isolating the benefit of communication through graph edges. The previous perceptual-loss, identity-loss, densification/pruning and geometry-coupling ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same distance-standard-deviation reporting. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests, and the new ablation introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds graph-disabled median/mean errors of 0.98/1.21 mm, versus the retained full-model result of 0.93/1.16 mm. All previous numerical table entries remain unchanged. Figures 1 and 4 replace qualitative reconstruction examples; different inputs prevent interpreting these as same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 rewrites Equation 5 using a diagonal scaling matrix instead of separate vector/matrix notation. Both formulations retain tangential scaling and normal-direction center offsets while keeping the 2D Gaussians flat. This is an equivalent clarification, without new assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about self-supervised Gaussian-based geometry learning, the UV/graph architecture, geometric coupling and benchmark performance. The rewritten conclusion preserves their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 newly interprets the graph-disabled result as evidence for the graph architecture. The conclusion also sharpens the existing alignment limitation by explaining that blurring compensates for misalignment and can limit Gaussian photorealism; scale and fixed-FOV limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the Gaussian parameter total to 14, consistent with the unchanged listed dimensions. Figure 2 adds an explicit legend identifying frozen, learnable and parameter-free modules, clarifying DINOv2's frozen status. These are documentation refinements rather than demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged. The rewritten binding passage preserves the same positioning as an anisotropic 2DGS adaptation of GaussianAvatars; AlbedoGAN was already cited and quantitatively compared in v1.

P1.justification: Localized rewriting affects the introduction's rendering terminology, the binding explanation, the ablation discussion and the conclusion. The section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 4 replace portrait examples, Figure 4 changes and reorders comparator columns, and Figure 2 is redrawn with a module-type legend. Table 4 gains a graph-enabled column and one row. These are localized display changes within the retained document layout.

improvement.justification: The new graph-edge ablation supplies previously missing evidence for a specific architectural choice, while the parameter-count correction, diagram legend and clearer binding and limitation explanations improve clarity. The gains are limited, with unchanged headline quantitative results. A small regression remains: Section 6.1 still lists Deep3DFaceRecon for Figure 4 even though the revised figure substitutes AlbedoGAN.
